Melatonin, a hormone believed to be involved in the main- tenance of circadian rhythms, may be useful in the treat- ment of insomnias such as those due to jet lag20 or other disorders (where it might act by resetting the body clock), and in the elderly. However, its benefits have been ques- tioned,21 and certainly evidence for a direct hypnotic effect is less conclusive; its sleep-inducing properties are usually only seen after very high, supraphysiological concentra- tions have been attained.5,6 Ramelteon, a melatonin recep- tor agonist, is used as a hypnotic in some countries. 1.
